Frequently Asked Questions
 Is Parking Available?
Yes, parking will be available in each of the Filoli parking lots.
 Is this wheelchair and stroller accessible?
Yes, the house and garden are accessible to wheelchairs and strollers. Wagons are not allowed. We have free wheelchairs located at the Guest Services booths*, please ask upon check-in.
*Free wheelchairs are pending availability and are provided on a first come, first serve basis. 
 Can I re-enter if I leave?
Yes, guests must show their wristbands upon reentry.
 I’m a member, what are my benefits for this event?
Membership benefits for this event as follows: 
All members
 receive free daytime admission to Holidays at Filoli, including Thistlewyck Village. Advance reservation is required, and tickets are subject to availability.
All members
 also receive 20% off up to 4 additional daytime admission tickets.
Filoli - Guild level members and above
 receive 20% off Holiday Lights (evening) tickets.
Circle, Family for All, and Community Family members 
receive free daytime and evening admission with no reservation required — even on sold-out days.
 What are the run times for the Holiday Events?
Daytime and Holiday Lights experiences are available from November 14, 2026 - January 10, 2027
Thistlewyck Village will be available from November 14, 2026 - January 3, 2027
 When does daytime admission end and evening admission begin?
Daytime runs from 10am - 3:30pm with the latest admission at 1:30pm.
Evening runs from 4pm - 10pm, with the latest admission at 8:00pm.
 Does Thistlewyck require a separate ticket?
No, Thistlewyck is a part of your daytime experience. To access Thistlewyck please reserve a Holiday Daytime Ticket. 
 Can I enter earlier than the time on my ticket?
No, you must enter at the selected time on your ticket. If you would like to change your entry time, please contact us at 
[email protected]
. to reschedule it. There is a $10 rescheduling fee per ticket.
 Can I enter later than the time on my ticket?
For a better experience, we recommend you enter at the selected time on your ticket. However, if you arrive later than the original time, you will be able to enter.
 Can I reschedule my tickets?
Tickets can be rescheduled by contacting 
[email protected]
.
 There is a $10 rescheduling fee per ticket. Please allow for up to 48 hours for us to process the reschedule request. 
 Are tickets refundable?
Tickets are non-refundable.
 Can I stay for the evening if I have General Admission?
Admission for daytime and evenings are different. Please purchase a Holiday Lights or a Holiday Lights Anytime + ticket if you are planning to stay.
 Will Quail Café be open?
The Quail Cafe is open daily until 9:30pm.
The cottages and bars in the Garden are open daily until 9:30pm.
 Will there be shops open?
The Clock Tower Shop is open until 10pm.
The Trail Head Store is open until 3:30pm.
 Does Museums for All (EBT) cover Holidays?
Yes, Holiday Daytime and Holiday Lights tickets are covered by Museums for All and Community Family membership. SNAP EBT cardholders receive 4 free admission tickets each day, and can book ahead by contacting 
[email protected]
.
Community Family and Family for All members receive 4 free adults and up to 6 children under 18 each day. 
 What do I do if it rains on the date I have tickets for?
Filoli is open rain, or shine. Tickets can be rescheduled by contacting 
[email protected]
.
 There is a $10 rescheduling fee per ticket. Please allow for up to 48 hours for us to process the reschedule request. 
 Help, I've lost my item! What do I do if I have lost an item at Filoli?
If you have lost or misplaced an item on our property during your visit, please email 
[email protected]
 or call our Guest Experience team at 650.364.8300 x231.

 IlluminOdyssey 10 
Inspired by the science of light, IlluminOdyssey is an immersive, interactive installation that will mesmerize kids and adults of all ages*. CuriOdyssey's four-level Redwood Hall will transform into a glowing forest of science—light your way through a maze of luminous botanical geometry, play with rainbow refraction and swirling projections, paint with light on phosphorescent surfaces, and dance with your shadow. Explore the physical properties of light, such as photoluminescence, color, additive light mixing, waves, fluorescence, fluid dynamics, subtractive color mixing, and refraction.
IlluminOdyssey is celebrating 10 years the only way we know how: bigger and better than ever. This milestone year brings 10 new glowing exhibits packed into Redwood Hall, with beloved favorites alongside dazzling new additions. This fan-favorite exhibition is free with admission or membership. CuriOdyssey's hands-on approach to science education influences every facet of this exhibition. IlluminOdyssey's interactive glowing exhibits awaken kids' curiosity, build critical thinking skills, and inspire an interest in science and the natural world. As a non-profit outdoor science museum and zoo, we make exploring science, technology, engineering, art, and math fun and exciting for kids and adults of all ages.
*Please note:
 This is a darkened hall with a variety of light-based exhibits and artwork. Visitors sensitive to light and sound may be affected. Learn more in our 
IlluminOdyssey Social Story.

First Friday Nights is lighting up the night to celebrate 10 years of IlluminOdyssey, and you’re invited to explore, create, and dance under the lights. First Friday Nights brings our community together for an evening of science, creativity, and connection. Paint with light, make a blacklight butterfly, and get a glow-in-the-dark face design.
Between activities, explore IlluminOdyssey 10. It has 10 new glowing exhibits in Redwood Hall alongside beloved favorites. Wander a maze of luminous botanical geometry, play with rainbow refraction, paint with light, and dance with your shadow.

 IlluminOdyssey 10 FAQ 
What is IlluminOdyssey 10?
IlluminOdyssey 10 is an indoor, interactive winter light exhibition for families at CuriOdyssey, a nonprofit science museum and zoo in San Mateo, California. It runs 
November 14, 2026–January 24, 2027.
 For its 10th year, CuriOdyssey's four-level Redwood Hall becomes a glowing forest of science, with 10 new exhibits alongside favorites from past years.
Is IlluminOdyssey okay for kids with sensory sensitivities? 
IlluminOdyssey is a darkened hall with light-based exhibits, and some areas have flashing lights and sound, which may affect visitors sensitive to light and sound. Sound dampeners and sensory tools are available at CuriOdyssey's front desk, and staff can help find a sensory-safe space. CuriOdyssey also hosts quarterly Sensory Sundays with fewer crowds; preregistration is required.
Is IlluminOdyssey educational? 
Yes. Every IlluminOdyssey installation explores how light works, including color mixing, refraction, fluorescence, photoluminescence, waves, and fluid dynamics. CuriOdyssey designed it to spark kids' curiosity and build critical-thinking skills through play, so it's both a holiday outing and a STEAM activity.
What age is IlluminOdyssey best for?
IlluminOdyssey is designed for kids and works for toddlers through tweens, and adults enjoy it too. For older kids, CuriOdyssey offers winter break day camps for ages 6 to 10, with themes inspired by IlluminOdyssey's 10th year.
What's new for IlluminOdyssey's 10th year?
IlluminOdyssey 10 adds 10 new glowing exhibits to mark its 10th season, alongside returning favorites. Families can expect a maze of luminous botanical geometry, rainbow refraction, swirling projections, light-painting walls, and shadow-dancing stages. IlluminOdyssey first opened at CuriOdyssey in November 2017.
When is IlluminOdyssey 10? 
IlluminOdyssey 10 runs November 14, 2026 through January 24, 2027 at CuriOdyssey, 1651 Coyote Point Drive, San Mateo, CA 94401.
What are IlluminOdyssey's hours?
During IlluminOdyssey, CuriOdyssey's winter hours are 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM daily, with last entry at 4:00 PM. 
How much are IlluminOdyssey tickets?
IlluminOdyssey 10 is included with CuriOdyssey general admission; no separate ticket is needed. Admission is $29.95 for adults (18–61) and $24.95 for children (18 months–17 years), students with ID and seniors (62+). Infants under 18 months and CuriOdyssey members get in free.
Are there discounts?
Yes. Families with EBT, SNAP or WIC get free admission through Museums for All. Military get 50% off with ID, and teachers get in free with a valid teacher ID. Reciprocal members of ASTC, AZA and ROAM may also qualify. Discount tickets are sold only on site, on the day of your visit.
Do I need to reserve tickets in advance?
Reservations aren't required, but we recommend reserving online. All tickets are for a specific date and time, and booking ahead cuts your wait. Members don't need a reservation; just show your photo ID at the admissions window.
What's the least crowded time to visit?
CuriOdyssey is busiest from 10 AM to noon. For a calmer IlluminOdyssey visit, come after 2 PM. Tickets have no time limit, so you can stay until closing.
Do members get special access?
CuriOdyssey members get free admission and free parking. Members are also invited to Member Mornings with breakfast, 8:30– 9:30 AM on November 21, 2026, and January 23, 2027 (RSVP required).
What else is there to do at CuriOdyssey?
IlluminOdyssey admission also includes CuriOdyssey's indoor science center, zoo, walk-through aviary, Nature Play Grove, Nature Play Garden, Bay Gallery and Whooosh! playground.
Is there an indoor holiday light show in the Bay Area for a rainy day? 
Yes. IlluminOdyssey 10 is fully indoors in CuriOdyssey's Redwood Hall in San Mateo, so rain and cold don't affect it. It runs daily from November 14, 2026, to January 24, 2027, with some holiday closures. CuriOdyssey's indoor science center is open the same day, so you can make a full visit without going outside much.
What are the best holiday light experiences for families in the San Francisco Bay Area? 
IlluminOdyssey 10 at CuriOdyssey in San Mateo is one of the Bay Area's top holiday light experiences for families with young children. It runs November 14, 2026–January 24, 2027. Unlike outdoor light walks and drive-thru shows, it's indoors, open during the day, and hands-on: kids touch, move, and play with the light. It's included with regular museum admission.
What's a good holiday light show for toddlers and preschoolers near San Francisco?
IlluminOdyssey 10 at CuriOdyssey in San Mateo works well for toddlers because it runs in the daytime, so the visit fits around naps and early bedtimes. Little kids can walk a glowing maze, dance with their shadows, and paint with light on glow-in-the-dark surfaces. Children under 18 months get in free. CuriOdyssey is just off Highway 101 in San Mateo, about 20 miles south of San Francisco.

What started as one man’s passion for bringing holiday joy to his community has grown into the Bay Area’s most beloved free Christmas celebration.
Our Story
In the 1950s, Don Lima borrowed $300 to build the first holiday display in San José. His single Nativity scene on his lawn sparked such community enthusiasm that it grew year after year, eventually becoming too large for his property.
Don donated his displays to the City of San José, and in the early 1980s, Christmas in the Park found its permanent home at Plaza de Cesar Chavez. Today, we’re a community-driven non-profit organization dedicated to keeping this magical tradition free and accessible to all.
More than 90% of our budget comes from community fundraising and sponsorships, ensuring that families from all backgrounds can experience the wonder of Christmas in the Park without cost barriers.

Frequently asked questions
 What is Christmas in the Park? 
Each year, the two-acre Plaza de San José is transformed into a holiday fantasy with over 40 musical and animated exhibits, glittering lights and the 60-foot Community Giving Tree. Some of the original displays are housed in one of the largest exhibits, the Lima Train, include a melting snowman, caroling mice and elf woodcrafters.
We are a 501 (c3) non-profit organization that brings this free community event through sponsorships, donations, grants, and programs. Each summer, we host “Christmas in July,” a fundraiser under the stars, where guests dine and dance in support of the event. Throughout the rest of the year, Santa and his elves work long and hard to clean, spruce and fix up the displays, work with companies to develop sponsorships, find grants, and raise the necessary dollars to bring this magical holiday experience to you every year.
 How much does it cost to go to Christmas in the Park? 
Admission is absolutely free! It costs nothing to visit Christmas in the Park with your friends and families. Donations are greatly appreciated and can be made online, in the Information Booth or Santa Visit Area.
 When is the park open? 
Christmas in the Park opens Friday, November 27, 2026. The event is open every day through January 3, 2027: Friday–Sunday, noon–10:00 PM; Monday–Thursday, noon–9:00 PM, including Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year’s Eve, New Year’s Day, January 2, and January 3.
 Where is Christmas in the Park? 
Christmas in the Park takes place in the heart of Downtown San José at Plaza de San José on Market St. between San Fernando and San Carlos St.
 How can I donate to Christmas in the Park? 
Simply choose the “Get Involved” tab on our home page and follow the simple donate instructions. There are also donation boxes in the Information Booth and Santa Visit Area.
To be put on Santa’s Good List, Leave a Donation! For Sponsors, please visit the sponsors page to learn more about the benefits of being a Christmas in the Park sponsor.
 Are there restaurants nearby? 
Of course there are! Christmas in the Park is located in the heart of downtown and is surrounded by multiple restaurants all within walking distance.
 Are there hotels nearby? 
Plenty of hotels border Christmas in the Park, but Santa’s home away from home is Signia by Hilton.
 Is there live entertainment in the Park? 
Daily entertainment kicks off on opening night. Check out our schedule of events!
 Is food available in the Park? 
The Christmas in the Park Food Court is located at the south end of the park near San Carlos St. Located in the north end of the park is “Santa’s Snack Shack” presented by the Downtown Kiwanis organization.
 How do I become a vendor at Christmas in the Park? 
Visit our 
vendor page
 for information on how to become a vendor.
 How can I sign up to perform on the stage? 
To be a part of the live entertainment, all acts must register online. All performances and costumes must be family-friendly and exhibit good taste. We welcome all kinds of acts, from singing, and dancing, to other unusual and fun talents.
 Forgot cash! Is there an ATM in the Park? 
Yes, there is. There is an ATM located at both the north and south ends of the park as well as at the crosswalk on the Signia Hilton side of the park and the crosswalk on the Tech Museum side of the Park. Remember, there is a fee for using the ATM.
 When will Santa be in the Park? 
Santa’s House hours will be posted on our Events page and within the Park. You can visit and take photos for free. Donations are always welcome.
 I want to help! How do I volunteer? 
It takes thousands of volunteer hours to make Christmas in the Park a reality. We offer a variety of volunteer opportunities ranging from a few hours a day to several weeks. Christmas in the Park is a popular choice for people in need of community service hours and students wanting to get more involved in the community. Choose the “Get Involved” link from our homepage for more information.
 How old do you have to be to volunteer? 
All volunteers under the age of 18 must have a Minor Consent form signed by a parent or guardian to participate in the student volunteer program. An adult supervisor is needed to accompany all students under the age of 16. All volunteers, regardless of age, must sign a volunteer service form before the start of the event.
 Are dogs allowed at the park? 
Dogs are allowed in the Park when on a leash and well tended to by their humans. Keep in mind weekend nights are very busy and may not be safe for your pets.
 Don’t forget to check out our social media sites! 
Follow us on Facebook and Instagram for up to date information and special announcements.
 What about the ice rink, rides 
The ice rink and carnival rides are not produced nor managed by Christmas in the Park. Downtown Ice is a program of the San Jose Downtown Association. The rides that stretch along Paseo de San Antonio are known as Winter Wonderland and is a private business. Together, all three of us make up Downtown for the Holidays. We help bring business, entertainment, and fun to Downtown San Jose each year.

Aviation Camp FAQs
What if the camp I am interested in is full?
Aviation Camp is a popular program and many sessions have already filled up. Parents are encouraged to use the online enrollment system to join the waiting list for the session that they are interested in as early as possible. There is no charge to join a waiting list, and credit card information is not required.
Most Aviation Camp sessions which fill early will eventually have new spaces available, sometimes due to changes and cancellations for individual campers who enrolled earlier, and other times due to increases in camp capacity that make many new spaces available at once. Camper changes may occur at any time up until the camp start date.
Whenever a space or spaces become available for any full camp session, invitations to enroll will be sent via email to waitlisted campers from support@actvityhero.com with the subject line “Waitlist Status: Spot Available at Aviation Camp”. These invitations are sent in the order that campers joined the waiting list. Each invitation will include a special link to facilitate online registration into the full session, and an expiration date and time through which the link is valid. In most cases invitations are valid until 9 AM the next day, after which the invitation will expire and a new invitation will be sent to the next camper on the waiting list. Parents who receive an invitation to enroll from a waiting list should enroll before the expiration date/time to secure their spot.
Please note that Hiller Aviation Museum Members do not receive preferential placement on Aviation Camp waiting lists, but may enroll at the discounted Member price if a space becomes available.
Unfortunately, we are unable to predict the likelihood of space opening in any particular Aviation Camp session. Thank you for your patience – and for your interest in the Aviation Camp program.
Can I change camp sessions?
Schedule changes/transfers will be accommodated on a 
space-available basis
 when requested at least twenty-one days before the camp start date. Changes are subject to a $25 processing fee. Changes cannot be made into full camp sessions. For full sessions, campers will be added to the waitlist at the latest position.
To request a cancellation or change, please email 
camp@hiller.org
 with your child’s full name, and enrolled camp topic and date. 
Want to change but the session you are interested in is full?
Add your child to the waitlist.
In the meantime, you can either:
Cancel the current registration for a refund (minus applicable processing fees). 
Wait to get a waitlist invitation and then email camp@hiller.org for a transfer. Registrant will be responsible for any balance due. If a refund is owed, it will be refunded minus a $25 processing fee.
Please remember that you have up to twenty-one days before the camp starts to request a refund minus the processing fee. No refunds are issued within twenty-one days of camp start date.

Gaze into the stars, exploring space, creating constellations, and making moonlight. Campers will experiment with all things radiant to celebrate IlluminOdyssey's 10th year!

Adaptations abound with bioluminescent biology, incandescent insects, and echolocation. Campers will explore light through plants and animals to celebrate the 10th year of IlluminOdyssey!

san-carlos-holiday-lights.text: Night of Holiday Lights Home Departments Parks and Recreation  Events Night of Holiday Lights events@cityofsancarlos.org 16th Annual Night of Holiday Lights! Join us downtown from 5:00 to 8:30 p.m. on Friday, December 4, 2026. Festivities will take place on Laurel Street, from San Carlos Avenue to Cherry Street, with the main stage located on Cherry Street.  This free community event features: Family Fun and Kids’ Activities Arts and Crafts Beer and Wine sales Hot Chocolate and Holiday Goodies Holiday Show, Festive Lights, and Snow Musical performances! Don't miss a spectacular lineup of performers at  Night of Holiday Lights this Friday, December 4, starting at 5:00 p.m.! Emcees  Lori & RJ kick off the celebration at 5:00 p.m., and Wild Child will take the stage from 6:30 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. Followed by... The Tide Note Singers  led by Emily Bender San Carlos Children's Theater Broadway Babies & Kids Case Circulo Cultural Peninsula Ballet Arts Tap Dancing Christmas Trees A Tribute to Michael Jackson With special appearances from  Santa Claus and the Snow Queen! Youth Vendors Calling all youth entrepreneurs (grades 4-12 & at least 9 years old)! Interested in applying to be a youth vendor at Night of Holiday Lights? Apply to become a youth vendor today! Applications are available now and must be submitted prior to November 13 at 11:59 p.m.  Please review the application closely with your child prior to submitting.  In preparation for this event, the San Carlos Youth Center is hosting a FREE Entreprenuership Workshop Series on Fridays from 4:00 p.m. - 5:00 p.m. from October 30 - November 20. If your child would like to attend and is in 4th grade and at least 9 years old, please sign up for San Carlos' After School Drop-In Program at cityofsancarlos.org/scyc . Please note that participation in the Entrepreneurship Workshop Series does not guarantee participation in the Night of Holiday Lights event.
